body: Specialty chemical companies sell chemistry know-how (fluorination, nitration, process efficiency) to global agrochemical, pharma, polymer and refrigerant makers, plus import substitutes into India. Profit comes from complex-chemistry custom synthesis (CSM) contracts, where margins and stickiness are highest, while plain intermediates are priced against China. Key metrics: volume growth, gross margin per kg, EBITDA margin, asset turns (1.0–1.5x for new plants, which is why capex is lumpy), capex in progress, CSM order book and customer count, working capital days, and product concentration. Cycle drivers: China supply (capacity overbuild and dumping in 2023–26), global destocking (2023–24), agrochemical channel inventory, crude and feedstock prices, anti-dumping duties, the US tariff gap against China, and the monsoon for domestic agrochemicals. Lead indicators: China PPI and chemical prices, DGTR anti-dumping notifications, US agrochemical channel commentary (Corteva, FMC), Indian chemical export data from the Commerce Ministry, IMD monsoon. Winners (SRF, PI Industries, Navin, Clean Science) climbed the complexity ladder, held proprietary processes and built multi-year innovator relationships. Losers were commodity-like intermediates priced off China, or one-molecule firms. Valuation: P/E 50–80x at the 2021 China+1 peak, de-rated to 25–45x in 2023–25. Nov 2026: ICRA (31 Aug 2026) sees domestic-led volume recovery, but global overcapacity caps prices. CRISIL expects only ~6% revenue growth in FY27. Traps: extrapolating China+1, and capex before contracts.

data.business_model: Custom synthesis/CSM contracts + specialty intermediates + import substitution; know-how and process cost are the moats.
data.current_state_nov_2026: ICRA (31 Aug 2026): domestic-led volume recovery, global overcapacity caps prices. CRISIL: FY27 revenue growth ~6%, margins pressured. Anti-dumping duties on 14 more Chinese chemical categories confirmed in Q1 FY27 (single source). US tariff on Indian agchem 18% vs 35% on China. Mixed Q2 FY27: India Pesticides revenue −21.6%, Sharda Cropchem PAT +23%.
data.cycle_drivers: China capacity/dumping, global inventory cycles, feedstock prices, trade remedies, monsoon (domestic agchem), innovator patent cliffs.
lead_indicators: DGTR anti-dumping initiations and final findings
Global agchem majors' channel inventory commentary
Commerce Ministry export data (organic chemicals HS 29)
traps: New-capacity revenue never reaching asset-turn guidance
Inventory gains in rising price markets reported as margin
Paying peak multiples on peak margins
data.valuation: P/E 50–80x at the 2021–early 2022 peak; 25–45x in 2023–25 after destocking. EV/EBITDA 15–35x. Troughs coincide with peak China dumping, which is when P/Es look high on depressed earnings.
data.valuation_note: Historical valuation ranges and peak/trough dates come from general market history and were not re-verified against index factsheets this session. Treat them as unverified. Only the current-state figures are tied to the dated sources listed.
data.value_chain: Crude/feedstock (benzene, toluene, fluorspar) -> basic chemicals -> intermediates -> specialty/AI -> formulator (global agchem/pharma). Margins rise with complexity and regulatory lock-in (CSM, fluoro specialties); commodity intermediates face China pricing.
data.winners_vs_losers: Winners: rising complexity, IP-like processes, customer stickiness, conservative balance sheets through downcycles. Losers: commodity intermediates, single-molecule concentration, debt-funded capex before contracts, aggressive inventory build.

title: Sector playbook: Indian specialty chemicals and agrochemicals
